newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Some Euro refiners cut runs in margins squee.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Some Euro refiners cut runs in margins squee.

text.p: Poor profit margins this week have forced a handful of European refineries to cut crude oil runs and others are considering similar action, oil company and trading sources said on Tuesday.
But most plants were still running normally and better gasoline prices had tempted others to defer a decision on whether to reduce crude throughputs until later this week, the traders said.

Confirmed refinery run reductions on Tuesday amounted to just 65,000 barrels per day (bpd), a fraction of the 750,000 bpd of European distillation capacity scheduled to close for spring maintenance this month.
The 14 European Union member countries have nameplate capacity of some 12.5 million bpd.
Texaco said it had decided to cut runs by 10 percent, equivalent to 14,000 bpd, at its share of the 400,000 bpd Rotterdam plant it runs with BP.
Universal cut runs by 15 percent to 50,000 bpd at it's 60,000 bpd refiner at Antwerp.
"Since yesterday, we reduced by 15 percent as the margins were terrible," a company official said.
The 370,000 bpd Shell refinery in Rotterdam was operating as normal but "they are looking closely at it," said a trading source.
"Because of the complexity we usually get a bit more time than the simple plants," he said, adding that a decision might be made towards the end of this week.
Portuguese state oil company Petrogal reduced by around 40,000 bpd at its 210,000 bpd Sines refinery.
KPC's Rotterdam refinery came down for a month's maintenance earlier this week.
A fully upgraded, or complex, refinery in Rotterdam currently makes less than $1 a barrel for processing Brent crude oil.
This compares to an average of about $1.50 over the past three months and levels well over $2 last September and October.
Other refiners have been toying with run cuts but temptingly firm gasoline prices in recent days appear to have delayed any further decisions.
"We haven't seen much evidence of run cuts. Margins have been poor but not the worst we've seen," said a trader at a refinery in Antwerp.
"We are thinking about it (cutting runs)," said a trader at a UK refiner.
The spread between gasoline and Brent crude for the second quarter this year jumped 25 cents a barrel to about $5.40 this week.
This is below average of more than $6 a barrel in the second quarter last year but is an improvement on sub-$5 levels which traded for much of last month.
Complex refiners are reluctant to cut runs when gasoline prices are strong because they need to re-coup the cost of expensive upgrading kit.
The gains on gasoline reflect some tightness in the Mediterranean where refinery closures for spring maintenance may eventually crimp production.
But sagging crude prices, pushed lower by a resumption of Iraqi exports, have helped keep refiners profitable.
A complex refinery in Italy refining Urals crude was making over $1 a barrel on Tuesday although those lacking upgrading capability have been running at a loss for much of this year.
Italy's biggest refiner, Agip, had not reduced crude throughputs at any of its plants.
"We may have optimised a little bit on crude here and there but we haven't cut runs," said a trading source.
Agip plans to shut the 100,000 bpd Gela plant for 35 days later this month but other maintenance is restricted to upgrading units.
Italian refiner Saras was trying to reduce crude runs by optimising planned maintenance shutdowns at it's 320,000 bpd refinery in Sardinia this month.
In Britain's Esso, Shell and BP refineries were all running normally. Elf 's UK Milford plant was down for maintenance until March 20.
The 175,000 bpd Mobil refinery at Coryton, part of the BP-Mobil joint venture, was due to shut for maintenance for 8 to 10 days on March 20.
In Scandinavia there were few signs of run cuts.
Statoil's Mongstad refinery in Norway was operating as normal. Shell's 81,000 bpd Gothenburg, Sweden refinery and it's 53,000 bpd Sola plant in Norway both.
In Spain, Petronor's 250,000 bpd refinery at Bilbao remains shut for repairs for another ten days.
